newsitem.title: USA: High Frequency names Cary Leahey top US economist.
newsitem.headline: High Frequency names Cary Leahey top US economist.

text.p: High Frequency Economics, a New York-based economic advisory firm, said on Thursday that it has named veteran Wall Street economist Cary Leahey as chief U.S. economist, effective July 1.

Leahey, who had been at Lehman Brothers for the past six years, replaces David Munro, who will still stay with the firm as a contributor on Washington policy and other topics and as an economic counselor.

"Lehman is a fine firm, but I was in a situation (there) where my future advancement was limited," Leahey told Reuters while vacationing in upstate New York. "I reached a point where I took (my career there) as far as it can go."
He said he left Lehman on good terms. "The people there were just great," he said. "I had no problems."
Ethan Harris, senior economist at Lehman, said he will take on much of Leahey's responsibilities until a replacement can be found. Harris said the firm is midway into the process.
In a news release, High Frequency said it made the move as a part of the global economics firm's coverage of financial markets.

"(Leahey) has an insider's viewpoint on the markets that's extremely rare among economists," said Arthur Rosenzweig, managing director of High Freqency in a statement. "He knows how to cut to the chase and he is not afraid to stick his neck out."
Leahey said that he looks forward to the change, which will put him in an office rather than being on the trading floor.

"Things will be quiet. I will have more flexibility in my schedule. No more getting in at 0730 EDT," he said. "I will follow the (U.S. bond) market closely, but I will not know the minute to minute (flows) on who is buying what."
He noted that the decision to go to High Frequency Economics was easy, in that he has known Munro since 1975 and Carl Weinberg, a senior economist, since the early 1970s.

Prior to his stint at Lehman, Leahey was director of economic forecasting for General Motors Corp. He also served as a senior economist at Shearson Lehman Brothers and Data Resources Inc, and was an economist in the U.S. Office of Management and Budget and in the Council of Economic Advisors.
He received his PHd and Master's in economics at the University of Pennsylvania and BA in economics at Clark University.
